summary: Oregon Dept. of Forestry three-story lookout 3 miles NNW of Bend: camp 1930s, new tower 1957, removed or destroyed 1981; site now private with no public access.

facts.design: Started as a camp; 10-ft pole tower with 7x7 cab and cabin added 1950; replaced 1957 by a three-story enclosed tower with 14x14 ODF cab
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1981 (sources differ on wording); site is on private property

staffing.status: seasonal lookout staff from 1937 to at least 1965 per Bend Bulletin items and district reports

access.note: firelookout.com says the site is on private property with no public access

events.note: New lookout station near Bend; Earl Updyke chosen as lookout (Bend Bulletin, July 16, 1937); earliest staffing item found
Lookout staffed for 150 days; Fred Bembrey worked it as lookout fireman for the state fire association
Cabin and 10-ft pole tower with 7x7 cab added
Quarter-acre grass fire about a mile and a half north of Shevlin Park, put out by fire fighters from the Tumalo lookout (Bend Bulletin, July 10, 1954)
Central Oregon District annual report: 20-foot laminated tower with standard 14x14 lookout house under construction; Brooks-Scanlon donated almost all structural lumber

Three-story enclosed tower with 14x14 cab replaced the 1950 pole tower; a September 7, 1957 Bend Bulletin item says John and Olive Allen had worked the site seasonally since 1951 and Mrs. Allen was the state lookout in the new tower
Lookout reported what would become the Cinder Butte fire, June 25, 1962
Busy fire season with nineteen first reports called in from the station
Register says removed in 1981; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1981; Forest Lookouts page says only Removed
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on May 14, 2011

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower was removed in 1981; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1981. Both give 1981, so the story reports both words. The Forest Lookouts page gives no date.

The register and firelookout.com say Oregon Department of Forestry; the 1957 newspaper item on the Forest Lookouts page calls the builder the Oregon State Board of Forestry. Same state agency under its earlier name; story uses ODF.

notes_for_editor: Access: firelookout.com says private property with no public access; the brief's unknown is replaced with private. A web search turned up a real-estate listing (landandfarm.com) saying the historic site of the former Tumalo Butte Lookout is offered for sale and describing a home and lookout tower on it; the fetch was refused (HTTP 403), so it is unverified and not cited. Editor may want to check the parcel before any today line goes beyond private with no public access. Removed vs destroyed in 1981 is a wording conflict. Staffing to 1965 rests on the 1965 weebly entry. Brief kind three_story and 2011 registration check out. No photos added.
